title: list_by_chat and list_by_chat_paged: ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC — id is ULID but not guaranteed monotonic
description: MessageStore list_by_chat and list_by_chat_paged order by (created_at DESC, id DESC). id is a ULID which encodes the timestamp in its high bits — for messages with the same created_at second, ULIDs sort in monotonic insertion order. The tie-break by id is correct and efficient. However get_position_in_chat uses a correlated subquery that mirrors this tie-break logic: (created_at > m.created_at OR (created_at = m.created_at AND id > ?2)). The id comparison uses text lexicographic order. ULID strings are 26 characters of Crockford base32 — they sort correctly as strings only if all characters use the same case. Crockford base32 uses uppercase. If any code path inserts a ULID with lowercase characters, the text sort breaks. This is a latent risk: the sort is only correct if all IDs are uppercase ULIDs.
